close_reason: Switched return type to impl Iterator<Item = &Finding> + '_; callers that need a Vec now collect() at the call site (which documents the allocation cost explicitly). Updated the two in-source test callers (Vec indexing -> .collect() + len(); .len() -> .count()). No downstream callers exist outside pkix-lint itself; cargo build --workspace --all-features clean. Commit b082a620.
description:
pkix-lint/src/report.rs:176-181 has `pub fn findings_at_or_above(&self, min_severity: Severity) -> Vec<&Finding>` that internally builds a transient `Vec` via `.iter().filter(...).collect()`. Every caller that wants to render or count findings allocates this Vec, even when they only walk it once and discard it.

Idiomatic Rust: return `impl Iterator<Item = &'_ Finding> + '_` so callers compose further (`.take(5)`, `.find`, `.count`, `.next`) without the round-trip allocation. Callers that genuinely need a Vec can `.collect()` themselves — that is one extra token at the call site that documents the allocation cost.

This is the canonical 'leaky abstraction' pattern from the iterators subsection of the review prompt: forcing callers to call a method and then iterate (instead of returning an iterator directly) hides the natural iteration pattern.

Additional carry: AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 wants result types to admit caller-side caching. A Vec<&Finding> with lifetime tied to &self forecloses on certain reusable-buffer patterns; an iterator over &Finding does not.

Fix is non-breaking-source for callers that already do `.iter()` / `for f in result` on the return value (works on both Vec and Iterator), and breaking-source only for callers that call Vec-specific methods (.len, indexing). At 0.x there are no published consumers, so the fix is free now and a major bump later.
title: EvaluationReport::findings_at_or_above returns Vec<&Finding> instead of impl Iterator
